Repository: https://github.com/rafalh/rust-fatfs
Crate SHA256: 05669f8e7e2d7badc545c513710f0eba09c2fbef683eb859fd79c46c355048e0
Verified against crates.io version metadata and the Cargo registry index on
2026-11-07 by Verification Intern. All 31 archive files were preserved and
verified unchanged before the Lead-approved unmodified planting baseline.
The path dependency in Cargo.lock does not carry a registry checksum; the
original archive checksum above identifies the source for these local changes.

The r86 host dependency enables the existing chrono feature for current local
timestamps on ordinary mounts. Reproducible disk planting passes its fixed time
provider explicitly; no vendored time-provider code was changed.

Local changes from 0.3.6:
- boot_sector.rs: checked BPB metadata/FAT arithmetic, table capacity, FAT32
  root/active-FAT validation, and the formatter's hidden-sector option.
- file.rs: checked cluster offsets, file positions and seeks; malformed chains
  and missing clusters return errors instead of panicking or ending silently.
- fs.rs: checked cluster addressing, explicit hidden-sector format option,
  cluster-count bounds passed to iterators, and backup FSInfo initialization
  and updates inside the reserved region.
- dir.rs: direct physical dot entries, checked directory-entry positions, and
  a dedicated append writer for empty directories. It validates canonical 8.3
  syntax; callers must ensure unique names and no concurrent directory changes.
  Ordinary create operations retain collision checks and LFN support.
- table.rs: data-cluster validation, reserved-number tail exclusion from
  allocation/free-space statistics, and bounded full-chain iteration with read
  errors propagated by free/truncate.

Review context:
https://github.com/rafalh/rust-fatfs/issues/123
The append writer avoids repeated directory scans when planting a new tree.
The existing next-free-cluster hint already supports sequential allocation and
is retained; no separate allocation cache was added.
https://github.com/rafalh/rust-fatfs/issues/56
https://github.com/rafalh/rust-fatfs/issues/72
The #56 arithmetic concern is present in 0.3.6. The #72 report links older
code; 0.3.6 already computes the in-cluster offset with modulo. Local changes
address the separate cluster-range and seek/error paths verified in this source.
https://github.com/rafalh/rust-fatfs/issues/64
The dirty-FAT/BPB long-name regression fixture checks directory attributes,
physical dot entries, file contents and remount behavior. It does not establish
a complete fix for the reported macOS/STM32 eject scenario. Existing dirty bits
are preserved; these changes do not perform fsck or certify arbitrary images.
